timeline.say: So here it is, running. A Mina wallet connected to the app, and the Flare account it owns.
The relayer builds and proves the zkApp transaction, then hands it back unsigned. Nothing moves until this wallet signs it.

caption.text: The relayer proves — and returns it unsigned

timeline.say: Then a second signature claims the FMINA on Flare. A Mina Schnorr signature, verified by a Solidity contract.
There it is on Flare. Fifty FMINA minted, authorised only by a Mina key.
Now trade it. Ten FMINA for FXRP on BlazeSwap, a real DEX with real liquidity. Approve and swap go out as one signature over an ordered batch, so no live approval ever sits between two transactions.
Swapped. The account knows nothing about BlazeSwap — it just executes a signed list of calls.
And back the other way. Burning the wrapped asset releases the original.
And the validator set it all rests on, read live from Flare — five recovered keys, and the policy root Mina holds itself.
The burn, on the Flare explorer.
Three assets, both directions, all delivered.
